title: A block ending in a literal is accepted as a Java annotation argument and its statements are discarded
oracle: the whole expression as a Java annotation argument, read back by reflection, must equal the same expression evaluated in a method body, or be rejected as not constant
generator: wave4/harness/fold/fold.py --evolved: form N (annotation argument) over the block production { val u_ = e; literal }
detail: @Ann(z = { println("side effect"); false }, i = { val u = 1 / 0; 3 }) class A compiles, and reflection reads z = false and i = 3. The statements of each block are never run and are not in the class file; the same block in a method body or a default argument prints, or throws ArithmeticException. An annotation argument must be a constant expression, and other non-constant arguments get 'annotation argument needs to be a constant'. The check in typedAnnotation (Typers.scala around line 4210) looks at the argument's type, and a block whose last expression is a literal has that literal's constant type. This is the annotation-argument instance of the block-with-constant-type family: the fix for EO6 keeps the statements of such a block in ordinary code, but here the tree is replaced by the constant. Ordinary code is unlikely to write this on purpose; it matters where an argument is produced by a macro or an inline helper.
fix_sketch: In the constant-argument check require the typed argument to be a literal or a pure constant-typed tree (treeInfo.isExprSafeToInline), else report the existing error. Source that passes an impure block as an annotation argument stops compiling.
scala3: absent (3.7.4 reports 'Annotation argument is not a constant' twice)
prior: EO6 and LZ2 (retronym/scala#606: Block { val r = ...; literal } folded to the literal) are the same family in ordinary code; no earlier finding covers annotation arguments
